stimulus.title: Three oxyacids and a carboxylic acid
stimulus.text: Structures are shown with the acidic hydrogen bonded to oxygen.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: HOCl is a stronger acid than HOI. Explain why, in terms of molecular structure.

rubric.point: Cl is more electronegative than I, so it withdraws more electron density from the O–H bond and stabilizes the negative charge of OCl⁻ more than OI⁻
accept: higher electronegativity of Cl stabilizes the conjugate base

parts.sample: Cl is more electronegative than I. It pulls more electron density away from the O–H bond and from the oxygen of the conjugate base, so OCl⁻ is more stable than OI⁻. A more stable conjugate base means the ionization equilibrium lies further right, so HOCl has the larger Ka.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Trifluoroacetic acid is a much stronger acid than acetic acid. Explain why.

rubric.point: The three electronegative F atoms withdraw electron density from the carboxylate group, spreading out and stabilizing its negative charge

parts.sample: The three highly electronegative F atoms pull electron density through the carbon chain away from the –COO⁻ group. This spreads the negative charge of CF₃COO⁻, which is already shared by two O atoms through resonance, even further, so the conjugate base is more stable and the acid ionizes more.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Equal concentrations of NaOCl and NaOI are prepared. Identify the solution with the higher pH. Justify your answer.

rubric.point: NaOI, because HOI is the weaker acid, so OI⁻ is the stronger base (Kb = Kw/Ka is larger) and produces more OH⁻
accept: NaOI; Kb of OI⁻ is larger

parts.sample: NaOI. Kb = Kw/Ka, and HOI has the smaller Ka, so OI⁻ has the larger Kb (4.3 × 10⁻⁴ vs 3.3 × 10⁻⁷ for OCl⁻). OI⁻ takes protons from water to a greater extent, giving more OH⁻ and a higher pH.
